chains.title: SPDEF binding is reduced at the alt allele near the TOX3 locus
chains.element: The variant is annotated in an enhancer feature, but the nearest reported dELS cCRE is 38 bp away and does not overlap the variant.

links.claim: SPDEF is a candidate because it is expressed and ChIP-bound over the variant in MCF-7, and its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger in-vitro binding to ref than alt at a strong modeled site. This does not establish allele-specific occupancy in cells.
The variant has an enhancer-feature annotation, while the nearby dELS cCRE is active in some ENCODE biosample(s) but does not overlap the variant; enhancer function at the variant is not established.
TOX3 is a nearby candidate target, but no supplied evidence connects this variant or nearby cCRE to TOX3 regulation.
SPDEF is expressed and has ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in MCF-7; these observations support this tested context, not breast tissue generally.
A SPDEF-mediated effect could matter to breast cancer if it alters a relevant target, but no supplied evidence links this variant to breast-cancer risk or establishes a causal disease path.

predictions: If this chain is correct, allele-specific SPDEF occupancy at the variant should be higher on G than A in an appropriate MCF-7 assay.
A regulatory effect of the base should depend on SPDEF; its direction on TOX3 expression is not specified by the binding result.
falsified_if: A well-powered allele-specific assay finds no SPDEF occupancy difference between G and A.
A reproducible allele-dependent regulatory effect persists unchanged after SPDEF perturbation.

links.claim: TCF7L2 is ChIP-bound over the variant in MCF-7. A QBiC-SELEX model mapped from TCF7L1 predicts stronger alt binding and a strong modeled alt site, but this is indirect evidence for a TCF7L2-specific allelic effect; TCF7L2 expression in MCF-7 is relatively low.
The variant has an enhancer-feature annotation, while the nearby dELS cCRE does not overlap it; regulatory function at the variant is unconfirmed.
TOX3 is a nearby candidate target, but the supplied evidence does not show that this element regulates TOX3.
TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant is reported in MCF-7, although its reported expression there is low relative to the other prominent candidates.

A TCF7L2-mediated effect could be relevant to breast cancer only if it changes a relevant target; there is no supplied evidence that this variant affects breast-cancer risk or has a disease-effect direction.

predictions: If this chain is correct, allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy should be higher on A than G, and the regulatory effect should depend on TCF7L2.
This predicts the opposite allele direction for TF occupancy from the SPDEF chain.
falsified_if: A well-powered allele-specific assay finds no greater TCF7L2 occupancy on A than G.

outcomes.outcome: A base-dependent regulatory effect that is reduced or lost after SPDEF perturbation.

next_experiment: After confirming that MCF-7 cells are heterozygous at rs56007086, perform targeted allele-specific SPDEF CUT&RUN or ChIP-qPCR across the site. It is the least costly direct test distinguishing the two highest-probability chains: H1 predicts no reproducible imbalance, whereas H2 predicts greater occupancy on G.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565398:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 79 occupied (16 with a strong site), 5 of 137 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 49 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 425 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 20 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
